author: BeauHD
description: A software bug at JPMorgan Chase has disrupted online banking services Monday, triggering transaction delays for thousands of customers at Chase and other major U.S. banks. "JPMorgan Chase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in an on-premise hardware system -- it is not cyber-related," said Joe Evangelisti, spokesman for the bank. "This is not a systemic issue -- other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," he added. The Associated Press reports: Monday's technical issues seem to be centered at Chase customers and customers at other banks trying to transact with Chase. Those banks, including Bank of America and Citigroup, were not having issues with their banking services. A spokesman for U.S. Bank said its systems are not directly impacted but that "clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays." Dev
title: JPMorgan Chase Glitch Disrupts Online Banking Across Major US Banks

author: BeauHD
description: AT&T is suing (PDF) Comcast over its "fiber-powered" advertising, arguing that the term misleads consumers into believing Xfinity offers fiber-to-the-home service when most customers actually receive their Internet through coaxial cable. "Comcast should be required to restore to AT&T any and all profits earned as a result of its false and misleading advertising or provide AT&T with any other restitutionary relief the Court deems appropriate," the lawsuit said. The lawsuit asked for a permanent injunction "requiring Comcast to cease describing its hybrid fiber-coaxial service as 'Fiber-Powered.'" Ars Technica reports: While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber throughout the US, its cable Internet service makes the final connection to homes with coaxial cable. This results in upload speeds being far slower than download speeds. In contrast, fiber-to-the-home service can provide symmetrical upload and download speeds. Comcast has deployed fiber-to-the-home in only small port
title: Comcast's 'Fiber-Powered Wi-Fi' Is Just Cable, AT&T Says In False Advertising Case

author: BeauHD
description:
The FBI is warning (PDF) that hackers are using the AI-powered penetration-testing tool Artex to compromise networks in "under three hours" in some cases. The tool has been linked to attacks against South Korean financial institutions, at least 2,250 ConnectWise customers and Barracuda. TechCrunch reports: Artex is one of several open-source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network's defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open-source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI says Artex intrusions can be "noisy," meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company's defensive alerts. But the tools allow hackers to move at speeds that makes it far more harder for human defenders to keep up.
 
In some cases, Artex-linked attacks can move from targeting a system to active compromise "in under three hours." Oftentimes, A
title: FBI Says Artex AI Open-Source Hacking Tool Used to Breach Networks In 'Under Three Hours'

author: BeauHD
description:
Slashdot readers djgl and Mirnotoriety shared a story about how a Microsoft Outlook outage contributed to a chlorine leak at Germany's Phantasialand theme park, injuring 15 guests, four of whom were hospitalized. German broadcasting institution WDR reports (translated to English): We were all affected by this problem: On Friday, there was a disruption that crippled the US software company Microsoft, including its email program Outlook. Phantasialand was also affected. Due to the disruption, no emails were received, as the company informed WDR on Saturday. As a result, no one was aware that the sauna area's maintenance safety system had already issued an email alert. This was because the automatic dosing system had pumped too much chlorine into the pool.
 
Guests at the Hotel Ling Bao in Phantasialand, Bruhl, were injured as a result. They complained of health problems after visiting the pool. The pool was temporarily closed but has since been reopened, as the fire department informed
title: Microsoft Outage Leads To Chlorine Gas Poisoning At German Theme Park

author: BeauHD
description:
Apple is reportedly targeting WWDC 2027 to unveil its first smart glasses, with shipments planned before the end of that year. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman (paywalled), the company has hopes of making them its flagship new product for 2027. Forbes reports: It's no secret that Meta with its Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta glasses, for instance, lead the field when it comes to smart specs. "Apple is counting on integration with the apps people already use on their iPhones to be a key differentiator for the glasses," Gurman said. The App Store has millions of apps while Meta's apps are far fewer. It seems the smart glasses will use a version of the software used on the Vision Pro.
 
"The thinking inside Apple is that while Meta has the increasingly popular Muse agent, Apple has the App Store. Because the Siri integrations are being developed for the iPhone first, software makers won't need to build separate applications for the glasses," Gurman insisted. It seems the glasses will do
title: Apple Eyes 2027 Launch For AI-Powered Smart Glasses

author: BeauHD
description: An anonymous reader quotes a report from ProPublica: When Stanley Black & Decker, one of the world's largest tool companies, got hit with President Donald Trump's tariffs last year, the firm made clear that it would be sharing the pain with its customers. The Connecticut-based company raised prices again and again, moves its executives said were necessary because of the new fees on imports. Now, after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's most sweeping tariffs earlier this year, the company is getting at least $298 million refunded. Instead of sharing that bounty with its customers, however, the firm has chosen different recipients: Its own leaders. The company is one of at least nine that have disclosed that they are using their refunds not to pay back the cash-strapped consumers who generally covered much of the tariff costs through higher prices, but to give bonuses, according to a ProPublica analysis of thousands of securities filings and earnings calls for publicly traded com
title: Corporations Are Using Trump's Tariff Refunds On Bonuses Rather Than Reimbursing

author: BeauHD
description:
Over the weekend, SpaceX successfully caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time, demonstrating a key piece of its plan for a fully and rapidly reusable launch system. The achievement means SpaceX has now demonstrated tower catches of both Starship stages, though not yet on the same flight. "Many small fixes are needed to achieve immediate reusability (like an airplane)," noted SpaceX's Elon Musk. The Register reports: Flight 15 began well, with the 33 Raptor engines of the Super Heavy booster launching the stack from Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas. Hot staging followed, and the booster performed its directional flip maneuver. Thirty-two Raptor engines relit for the boostback burn, intended to return Super Heavy to the tower for another catch. The booster had managed the maneuver on flight tests 5, 7, and 8, but this time something went wrong. "The boostback burn ended early due to low fuel mass," SpaceX said.
 
The booster automatically aborted its return to the
title: SpaceX Catches Starship On the First Try

author: BeauHD
description:
Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as the next James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig as 007 and ending months of speculation over actors including Callum Turner, Nicholas Hoult and Jack Lowden. Denis Villeneuve will direct the new Amazon MGM film, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay.
 
"James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "I'm deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team." Variety reports: Pattinson picks up the 007 mantle after Daniel Craig's five-movie run as the womanizing super spy, which began in 2006 with "Casino Royale." Craig's final turn was in 2021's "No Time to Die," which ends with Bond sacrificing himself to save the world from a secret glo
title: Robert Pattinson Named As New 007

author: BeauHD
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Forbes: In a statement published on Monday, the Commerce Department said a new interim rule will address "rapid advancements in cloud computing" that have made it easier for countries like China to access advanced AI chips under export controls, including by accessing them remotely in data centers located in countries not under U.S. export controls. The new rule will require an additional license to export, reexport or transfer chips to companies in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Brazil, or any other country the U.S. deems a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion."
 
Last week, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after admitting to having an affair, which was linked to a relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence asset and a former executive at Singaporean data center firm Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer that was previously under suspicion for allowing China access to the company's advanced AI chips. The news com
title: US Closes Loophole That Allowed China To Remotely Access Nvidia Chips

author: BeauHD
description: Microsoft says last week's massive Microsoft 365 outage was caused by a software defect introduced in a July update that remained dormant until a Teams failover and a simultaneous 14% reduction in gateway capacity triggered a cascading failure. More than 80% of the affected gateway servers became unresponsive at the outage's worst point, and because the months-old change could not simply be rolled back, engineers spent roughly 15 hours developing and deploying a patch that restored the previous code path. The Register reports: According to a preliminary post incident report published by Microsoft on November 15, the defect was introduced in July 2026. The update looked fine at the time, Microsoft says, having passed load testing and been deployed without any impact. However, the testing wasn't good enough. Microsoft's report states: "Our load testing tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores." The defect caused "lock contention inside an internal Windows process which caused
title: Microsoft Blames Monster Email Outage On Software Defect Introduced In July Fix

author: EditorDavid
description:
The blog XDA Developers reports that a Claude enthusiast used the AI assistant to make a language model that runs off a floppy disk. "And you can stick it on a DOS computer to boot." 

The language models "runs at a respectable speed, given that it's running off a CPU that was designed decades before LLMs were even a thing."




Over on the ClaudeAI subreddit, user wollymonjak showed off this really impressive feat... [I]t's not going to be a particularly powerful AI; in fact, wollymonjak notes that if you ask something too complex or too long, it starts spitting out nonsense. But who cares about that when you're using a language model on DOS?
 


The same blog also notes that "the iPhone Duo hasn't been out for too long, and someone has already gotten Windows 11 on it."

As spotted by TechSpot, this cool feat was performed by Ammaar Reshi over on X. Their project is called WindowsiOS, and its goal is to get Windows 11 running on an iPhone Duo without jailbreaking. Usually, when we co
title: AI-Assisted Coders Run Windows on iPhone Duo, Build a Floppy Disk-Based AI Chatbot for MS-DOS

author: EditorDavid
description:
From the Linux-news blog OMG Ubuntu:


Purism is crowdfunding a new version of its Librem 5 Linux smartphone, this one powered by RISC-V rather than Arm. 

Librem 5 v2 will use an octa-core SpacemiT K1 RISC-V SoC, replacing the quad-core Arm64 NXP CPU. This processor shift will provide better performance and longer battery life than the original Librem 5 and not run as hot in use. Memory is bumped to 8 GB RAM, up from 3 GB, and storage leaps to 128 GB from 32 GB. Librem 5 v2 will run PureOS, Purism's Debian-based operating system using Phosh as its UI. SD card read speeds are faster, which is handy since the device can boot a second OS from a memory card. On-board hardware encoding means the Librem 5 will be able to take 13 megapixel photos and shoot high-definition video for the first time.... 

"RISC-V is the future, and Librem 5 v2 is the perfect product to bring it to a mainstream audience", Jonathon Hall, CTO at Purism, says of the launch.
"Freeing us from the control of Big Tech
title: Purism Announces 'Librem 5 v2' Linux Phone with RISC-V SoC

author: EditorDavid
description:
United Launch Alliance's new heavy-lift Vulcan rocket "malfunctioned while climbing into space yesterday," writes Engadget, "destroying its payload of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites..."


Launch failures are always a risk, but amazingly, United Launch Alliance had never experienced one previously. Since the company formed in 2006 as a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, its Atlas V rocket has been famously dependable. Now, the company's more powerful, more complex Vulcan will be under review by engineers and is facing a possible grounding... 



As well as being a major setback for United Launch Alliance, the failed launch will be a blow to Amazon's Leo internet satellite system, intended to rival SpaceXSI's Starlink network. Leo has 38 Vulcan flights booked to launch its satellites, following eight successful Atlas V missions. Many of those are now likely to be delayed. Amazon's other launch provider, Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin, suffered its own setback in May when its Ne
title: ULA Vulcan Rocket Failure Destroys 40 Amazon Leo Satellites

author: EditorDavid
description:
Romance novelist Coral Hart publishes her own romance novels for the Kindle, and found a kind of superpowere when she realized "the algorithm favours those who can produce a new book at least once a month," reports The Guardian:


 Hart says she knows of authors who hire more than a dozen ghostwriters to keep pace. By herself, Hart can write 10,000 words a day, but AI could help her produce many more. Since 2025 she has written 370 novels under 21 pen names using AI, earning herself "high six figures". Like any Kindle Unlimited author, she is only paid per pages read: it would make no business sense for her to churn out books that readers quickly abandon... "So, it's not taking the human out of the equation. It's taking the friction and the time and the business blocks out of the way." 

One study (awaiting peer review), led by Tuhin Chakrabarty of Stony Brook University, estimates that around one fifth of recently self-published books contain at least 25% AI-generated text. Hart now
title: AI-Generated Books Confront Publishing Industry With Big Questions

author: EditorDavid
description:
"Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive," reports Reuters, "and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter."


One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House... 

The report comes days after the FT reported that Nvidia's board had approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. 

The Guardian adds that Friday two major Nvidia shareholders "urged the board to keep 'all options' open."

In Washington, however, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent argued on Sunday that Nvidia should look "outside" the company for its next chief. "They need a dramatic shake-up," Bessent said on Fox News. Bessent also called on Nvidia to explain whether it knowingly allowed it
title: Should Jensen Huang Return as Nvidia's CEO? Supporters and Critics Disagree

author: EditorDavid
description:
Though the nationwide flight-grounding ended Friday, "Nearly 2,300 flights in the U.S. have been cancelled Sunday in the aftermath..." reports ABC News. "Additionally, some 18,689 flights were delayed, per FlightAware." 

But "a single malfunctioning FAA router in rural Arkansas appears to have caused the air travel chaos,"
reports the New York Post:



The problem originated at an FAA radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where a newly installed router flooded the network with excessive data traffic, disrupting communications between pilots and air traffic controllers, the Wall Street Journal reported. "We saw two places that were actually pinging our network at a very high rate, a thousand connections over every four to five seconds," Rebecca Guy, the FAA's technology chief, said on Saturday. .. [U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean] Duffy said the failure occurred during routine maintenance to replace aging copper telecommunications with fiber-optic cables — part of a broader effo
title: FAA Router In Middle-of-nowhere Arkansas Identified as Cause of Nationwide Flight Chaos
